Lispex 1.21.2 - Third-party notices for native executables
========================================================

Lispex is distributed under Apache-2.0. See LICENSE and NOTICE.

This inventory covers the union of normal Cargo dependencies for the
lispex executable, with default features and scored-native-contract, on:
  - aarch64-apple-darwin
  - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
  - x86_64-apple-darwin
  - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
  - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

Dependency selection uses cargo metadata --locked --offline with each
target filter, checked against cargo tree for the executable package
and release features. Development dependencies, build-only tools, and
procedural macro crates used only during compilation are excluded.
Dependencies that also have a normal dependency path are retained.

This is a dependency inventory, rather than a symbol-by-symbol account
of the linked files. Link-time removal and conditional code inside a
crate can reduce the code present in an individual executable. License
and notice files for bundled third-party code are included when shipped
within a selected crate. Rust toolchain components are outside this
Cargo dependency inventory.

For each third-party crate, the declared license expression is followed
by the full bundled LICENSE*, COPYING*, and NOTICE* files, recursively
and case-insensitively matched. Full text is retained; line endings
are normalized to LF and trailing spaces and tabs are removed.
Where a crate ships no such file, the entry is explicitly marked and
contains the standard SPDX text for each license and exception in its
declared expression. Standard MIT text retains SPDX copyright
placeholders because those packages did not bundle attribution text.
Expressions containing OR retain their alternatives; including all
texts does not change OR to AND. Legacy MIT/Apache-2.0 declarations are
reproduced as declared.

Third-party crate/version entries: 130
